title: Ghost traffic safety funnel and tenant-aware duplication controls
creator: Marco Silva
description:
Goal: Build a non-invasive 'ghost traffic' funnel that duplicates a sampled subset of production requests to candidate model lanes while guaranteeing tenant isolation, hard budget caps, and transparent telemetry. This ticket implements the runtime and controller pieces for safe request duplication, dynamic sampling policies, and cost enforcement so we can run large-scale shadow experiments without exposing customers to regressions or runaway cloud spend.

Scope:
- Runtime proxy changes to support lightweight duplication with minimal added latency to the primary path (optimistic fast path + async mirror where possible).
- Pluggable sampling engine (rate, stratified by tenant and request-class, adaptive ramp-up).
- Per-tenant budget accounting and early-quarantine circuit to stop mirrors when cost thresholds are reached.
- Tenant-aware isolation: mirrors must never leak state or alter downstream side effects; ensure idempotent headers, strip cookies, and enforce no-write mode by default.
- Observability: new metrics (mirror_rate, mirror_cost_per_tenant, mirror_drop_reasons), traces with mirrored-span children, and dashboards for SRE/PM.
- APIs: admin controls for per-tenant mirror budgets and global emergency kill-switch.
- Rollout model: feature-flagged canary (server-side flag + console toggle) with automatic rollback triggers based on latency/regression guardrails.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Async mirror write (fire-and-forget) minimizes p99 impact on primary path; we will fall back to sync duplication for routes that require immediate parity in trace propagation.
- Sampling supports both uniform and stratified modes. Stratified sampling is required to ensure low-volume tenants are represented. A default stratified policy will be created for the first rollout.
- Budget enforcement is implemented at the gateway (token-bucket per-tenant) to provide immediate stopping power. We accept that the gateway will occasionally over-count due to race windows; to mitigate we reconcile with post-hoc billing jobs and conservative budgets.
- Full payload redaction will be available via policy labels to protect sensitive tenant data when mirrors are enabled.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Proto change: add Mirror-Control headers and Mirror-Tags to request proto (backwards compatible).
2) Runtime proxy: implement mirror queue, async worker pool, and backpressure strategies. Ensure the mirror queue is bounded and drops with reason when full.
3) Sampling service: implement stratified sampler program with per-tenant config in config store (console-managed UI later).
4) Budgeting: implement per-tenant token-buckets + quotas; add emergency global kill-switch.
5) Telemetry & alerts: expose mirror-specific metrics and build dashboards; add alerting for sudden mirror cost spikes or mirror_error_rate > threshold.
6) QA & perf: microbench p99 impact < +3ms for common paths; e2e tests for no side effects.
7) Rollout: start with internal-only tenants, then opt-in customers, then wider canary controlled by console toggle with automatic rollback conditions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Mirrored requests can be enabled per-tenant and per-route via flags.
- End-to-end p99 latency impact on primary traffic is <= +3ms in 95% of routes measured.
- Per-tenant mirror budgets stop duplication within 5s of threshold breach.
- Mirrors cannot modify downstream state and are verified by integration tests.
- Console displays mirror_rate, mirror_cost, and mirror_drop_reasons per-tenant.
- Auto-rollback triggers defined: mirror-induced latency regression >5% p95 over baseline for 10 minutes OR error-rate delta on mirrored path >1% absolute for 5 minutes.

Open questions:
- Do we allow synchronous mirrors for any route at launch, or defer to post-launch? (risk: adds p99 overhead).
- Which default stratification keys to use for low-volume tenants? customer_id + route? We will A/B two variants in staging.
- Reconciliation window for budget counters: immediate or eventual? Current plan: immediate stop at gateway + nightly reconciliation job.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: /pages/REDACTED/GhostTraffic-Funnel (design + perf numbers)
- GitHub: draft PR at github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1423 (runtime changes), infra/pull/1428 (sampling service)
- Dashboard mockups in Drive: /drive/folders/REDACTED/mirror-dashboards

Long-term notes: support for sampled payload snapshots (scrubbed) to feed offline evaluations and drift checks; tie into Optimize to recommend mirror rates for cost vs. coverage trade-offs.

2025-02-21 Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed header and payload redaction plan. Recommend default strip of Authorization and Cookie headers and require opt-in for full payload mirroring (security_review_required=true).

2025-02-25 Michael Chen (Billing): Prototype budget token-bucket looks good. Concern: cross-region billing reconciliation — adding daily job to reconcile will mitigate over-charges. Filed billing task ENG-60201.

2025-03-01 Ayesha Kapoor: Added stratified sampler variant B to staging. Early results: low-volume tenants represented at 3x higher selection rate which improved regression detection in tests. Preparing canary with internal tenants next week.
2025-03-03 Marco Silva: Updated ticket with rollout plan and automatic rollback thresholds. Console toggle prototype ready — QA scheduled for 2025-03-06.
